exposure: Professional breastfeeding support (in-hospital guidance, MCHC follow-up post-discharge)
Demographic variables (first-time mother, ethnicity - Jewish vs Arab)
Pregnancy and birth details (preterm birth, low birthweight, cesarean birth, NICU hospitalization)
cohort: A convenience sample of 868 mothers attending Maternal and Child Health Centers in Israel up to three months post-partum.
finding: Even in a population with high initiation rates, the mean duration of exclusive breastfeeding was 66.8 days, which is less than recommended, and this duration was shorter for women with preterm births, low birthweight infants, cesarean births, and NICU hospitalizations.
mod_finding: Cesarean births were associated with a shorter duration of exclusive breastfeeding.
birth_weight: Low birthweight infants (LBW) were associated with a shorter duration of exclusive breastfeeding.
gest_age: Preterm births were associated with a shorter duration of exclusive breastfeeding.
